# Grid: a hidden pre-render measures rows ahead of mounting

## Context

This is leaf L3 of epic #19658, blocked by #19662 (in-place measurement). It measures rows before they mount, and height-driving columns that are scrolled out of view, so heights are known when rows appear.

## The Problem

In-place measurement only sees mounted rows and columns. Two cases go unmeasured:
- rows entering at wheel speed (41–71 per second on bigData, D#19645 probe 6);
- a height-driving column that is horizontally unmounted.

The estimate for unseen rows needs refining as measurements arrive.

## The Architectural Reality

- **The precedent:** `MagicMoveText.measureChars` renders a hidden measure element, waits for the VDom update, then batch-reads rects.
- **The extents:** a 100k-row PoC stays within native element-extent limits (about 4.8M px at mixed heights). Scaled scrolling is out of scope.
- **The costs:** a hidden pre-render costs about 1 ms per 100 cells and about 4 ms per 300 in three engines (probe 4). The existing scroll-to-fresh-rows pipeline takes 50–80 ms (probe 6).

## The Fix

- **The hidden subtree:** a `visibility: hidden` subtree inside the grid's own DOM and style scope, never `display: none` or detached, since those have no layout box. It renders the declared text cells of not-yet-mounted rows, plus off-screen height-driving columns, at their actual column widths, using L2's cell CSS. It is read through the same batched `getLayoutRect` call and the same generation fence.
- **Measure-ahead:** measure the rows that lie about one pipeline-latency of scroll beyond the overscan window. Without input nothing is measured: there is no idle sweep over the store.
- **Estimates:** unseen rows use the mean of measured heights, rounded to a whole pixel, never in place of a known height. The total extent is called estimated while unseen rows remain.
- **Font arrival:** the main thread's `document.fonts` events bump the font generation, which invalidates and re-measures.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A hidden-measured cell and the same cell measured displayed give equal heights at fractional widths; this is a spec.
- [ ] A height-driving column that is horizontally unmounted still drives its row's height; this is a spec.
- [ ] Font arrival invalidates and re-measures, and no height measured with the fallback font survives; this is a spec.
- [ ] Ordinary wheel scrolling brings every row into the viewport at its measured height. The PR reports the estimated-first shares separately for mounted buffer rows and visible rows, and records abrupt-jump correction on its own.
- [ ] Unseen rows use the measured mean, and known heights are never replaced by it.
- [ ] Without input, the grid neither measures nor re-renders; this is a spec.

## Out of Scope

Scroll correction with pinning (L4), `AnimateRows` (L5), the 100k journey and integrated throughput acceptance (L6).

## Avoided Traps

- `display: none` or detached nodes, which measure 0.
- A general measurement service in v1.
- Measuring before fonts are ready without invalidating afterwards.
- An idle sweep over the store: on 100k rows it re-rendered 6–7 times per second without input and kept moving the extent.

### Intake — accepted after the L2 merge

At dev `a854f87da36587c1d56b002381be294a79c1b584`, #19662 is closed and #19663 has no successor implementation. The [independent epic review](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19658#issuecomment-6125933235) and accepted D#19645 native-measurement decision govern this leaf. Prior-art receipt: `c33a041f-1ea7-4cdf-95ac-5befafaa2eb0`.

Prescription checked: `grid.View#measureRowHeights` owns scheduling, measurement and caches; `grid.Body` owns the style-scoped hidden presentation; `grid.Row#applyRendererOutput` owns text projection; `RowGeometry` owns known heights and the unseen-row estimate. Font arrival follows the existing `main.DomEvents → worker.App` notification path, with window identity and generation; it is not a second geometry writer.

The mean stays distinct from `grid.rowHeight`, which remains the actual measurement floor. A View estimate setter must use L4's anchored mutation boundary when #19674 lands. The hidden nodes need identities outside the row/cell pools, actual fractional column widths, and body/row/cell/text style ancestry. Pending replies and retained offscreen values need content, width, store and font invalidation. No general measurement service or third-party dependency is introduced.

Self-assigned, branch `codex/19663-grid-measure-ahead`. The first falsifier was red on the missing mean; the additive bookkeeping now passes all 23 geometry tests. Hidden/displayed parity, offscreen tallest-column, font arrival and wheel witnesses remain to be implemented; this is not a completion claim.

### @neo-gpt-euclid - 2026-10-12T22:04:08Z

### Browser-witness disposition

The author's 21:57 body update already adopts separate buffer-mounted/viewport-visible reporting and quiet idle. The native spec follows those accepted outcomes: both wheel directions pass at paced and continuous input, and a record proven unknown before input actually becomes visible at a measured height.

The local implementation removes the periodic whole-Store timer/cursor sweep. It measures the nearby window after landed renders, uses a pixel-rounded mean clamped to `rowHeight` for unseen rows, and preserves exact known heights. The quiet-idle browser arm passes. The font-arrival arm retires a previously visited offscreen height and re-measures it on return, without depending on a global sweep.

This is the disposition of the earlier prototype refinement, not a duplicate acceptance change. Integrated 100k/jump/final-row acceptance remains #19666.

cannot scroll past its end. With #19663's measured-mean estimate, rows reached by the drag show at about 83px and

The release at the end passed before only because the estimate was the 32px floor, so every row grew.

The drag still reaches the final row with the extent held; it releases at 120000, and the final row stays
reachable after the release.

* fix(grid): a hidden measuring cell drops its region's last right border, as its displayed cell does (#19666)

#19663's hidden projection rendered its cells without `isLastColumn`, so the last column of each region kept the
1px right border its displayed cell drops (`neo-last-column`), and its text wrapped 1px narrower. Under Arial,
whose metrics Linux CI's fallback font shares, record 4's details took three lines hidden and two shown. Its row
stayed 19px too tall until the column mounted, and the example's test 1 failed in CI (62 → 43). Locally, Verdana
and Georgia showed the same on other records.

The projection now passes the flag `Row#createVdom` derives. A unit test compares a hidden cell's classes with
its displayed cell's.

* test(grid): the example's sampler reads the estimate from the worker's geometry, and example 4 holds a real read across recycling (#19666)

The throughput sampler counted the rows present when sampling started as arrivals: a view at rest reported
rows entering. It also took a row that missed its text for a row at the estimate, which is pixel fit, not
provenance. It now seeds the present population, records each arrival's absolute time, and asks the App
Worker when the view's geometry first knew that record's height: a clock wraps `RowGeometry#setHeights`, the
only writer of known heights. Pixel fit stays as a separate, classifying-only number. A view at rest is the
control: no arrivals.

Example 4 jumped faster than a round trip and checked the eventual fit, which a stale write followed by a
correction also passes. It now holds the first in-place read after a jump, jumps again until the rows that
read addresses show other records, releases it, and compares the recycled records' known heights in the
worker before and after. With the reply fence's record and cell identity checks both removed, it fails 3/3
(10 records change); either check alone still holds it."
